fullTextEN: I am Sika from Taiwan.
How are you?
Welcome to Lazy Chinese.

fullTextZH: 今天我要说说关于名字的故事。
fullTextEN: Today I want to talk about the story of names.

fullTextZH: 我在网络上看到一个故事：
fullTextEN: I saw a story online:
There is a Chinese girl,
Her name is Zhaodi.

fullTextZH: 这个名字是爸爸妈妈取的，
fullTextEN: This name was given by her parents,
It was given by her parents.

fullTextZH: 这个名字有一个特别的意思。
fullTextEN: This name has a special meaning.
After Zhaodi grew up,

fullTextZH: 知道了这个名字的意思。
fullTextEN: She learned the meaning of this name.
At school,
At the workplace,

fullTextZH: 大家听到她的名字就会笑她。
fullTextEN: Everyone laughs at her when they hear her name.

fullTextZH: 所以招娣非常不喜欢这个名字。
fullTextEN: So Zhaodi really dislikes this name.

fullTextZH: 如果你不喜欢自己的名字，
fullTextEN: If you don't like your own name,
What would you do?
Can you change your name?
In China, you can change your name.

fullTextZH: 所以招娣就去改名字了。
fullTextEN: So Zhaodi went to change her name.
After changing her name,

fullTextZH: 她说她好像一个全新的人。
fullTextEN: she said she felt like a completely new person.

fullTextZH: 我看到这个故事的时候觉得很惊讶，
fullTextEN: I was surprised when I saw this story,

fullTextZH: 因为招娣是一个传统的中文名字，
fullTextEN: because Zhaodi is a traditional Chinese name,
it's a very old name.
It's now rarely seen in Taiwan,

fullTextZH: 应该不会有年轻人叫招娣。
fullTextEN: young people probably wouldn't be named Zhaodi.
Only the older generation,
like my grandmother,

fullTextZH: 那个时候的女人才叫招娣。
fullTextEN: women from that time were called Zhaodi.

fullTextZH: 现在我发现在中国还有很多年轻人叫招娣，
fullTextEN: Now I find that in China there are still many young people named Zhaodi,
and they all want to change their names.

fullTextZH: 现在你来猜猜：招娣这个名字是什么意思呢？
fullTextEN: Now you guess: what does the name Zhaodi mean?

fullTextZH: 为什么招娣都想改名字呢？
fullTextEN: Why do all the Zhaodis want to change their names?

fullTextZH: 招就是要东西过来的意思，
fullTextEN: Zhao means to summon something over,
Di is the 'di' in 'didi' (younger brother).

fullTextZH: 所以招娣这个名字的意思就是要弟弟过来。
fullTextEN: So the meaning of the name Zhaodi is to summon a younger brother.

fullTextZH: 如果父母给他们的女儿叫招娣，
fullTextEN: If parents name their daughter Zhaodi,

fullTextZH: 就是希望她能带来一个弟弟，
fullTextEN: it means they hope she can bring a younger brother.
I hope next time I can have a son.
If it were you,

fullTextZH: 你的爸爸妈妈给你取这种名字，
fullTextEN: Your parents gave you this kind of name,
What would you think?
This girl named Zhaodi,

fullTextZH: 大家听到她的名字都笑她，
fullTextEN: Everyone laughed at her when they heard her name,
They all asked her:
Did you bring a younger brother?
It made her very embarrassed,
and very unhappy.
Besides Zhaodi,

fullTextZH: 还有很多类似差不多的名字，
fullTextEN: there are many similar names,
such as Laidi and Pandi
all have the same meaning

fullTextZH: 就是希望下一个孩子是男孩。
fullTextEN: which is hoping the next child is a boy.

fullTextZH: 这就是中国重男轻女的文化。
fullTextEN: This is the Chinese culture of valuing boys over girls.
Valuing boys means valuing males,
thinking males are more important,
more useful.
Valuing girls less means undervaluing females,
They think girls are relatively unimportant,
relatively useless.
In the past, China was an agricultural society,
everyone farmed,
men were relatively stronger,

fullTextZH: 所以大家都比较想要生儿子。
fullTextEN: so everyone preferred to have sons.

fullTextZH: 而且只有男生可以继承家产
fullTextEN: Moreover, only boys could inherit family property
and inherit the surname,

fullTextZH: 就是只有儿子可以拥有爷爷和爸爸留下来的钱和姓。
fullTextEN: meaning only sons could have the money and surname left by grandfathers and fathers.

fullTextZH: 所以大家就觉得男生比较重要。
fullTextEN: So everyone thought boys were more important.

fullTextZH: 以前在台湾还有一种女生的名字，
fullTextEN: In the past, in Taiwan, there was a type of girl's name,
called Wangshi or Wangyao,

fullTextZH: 这些名字在台语的意思是随便养，
fullTextEN: these names in Taiwanese mean 'casually raised',

fullTextZH: 就是他们不想要生女宝宝，
fullTextEN: meaning they didn't want to have baby girls,
but now they have a girl,
there's nothing they can do,
just raise them casually,
let them grow up casually.
Hmm,

fullTextZH: 我为以前的女生觉得好难过，
fullTextEN: I feel so sad for the girls in the past,
They are not valued,
and they don't have nice names.
However, society is progressing now,
getting better and better,

fullTextZH: 这种重男轻女的想法越来越少了。
fullTextEN: and the idea of valuing males over females is becoming less common.
Regarding the culture of valuing males over females,
what do you feel?
Also,

fullTextZH: 你觉得名字重不重要呢？
fullTextEN: do you think names are important?

fullTextZH: 你的名字是什么意思呢？
fullTextEN: What does your name mean?
Is there a story?
Feel free to leave a comment and share!
See you next time.
Bye!
